new_statements.quote: En todos los demás casos, no se indica el tono aun cuando probablemente todos los dialectos lo tienen. El proto-idioma seguramente tuvo, aparte del tono, un acento sobre la raíz, que distinguía a ~sta de los afijos. En algunas partes de la comunidad dialectal pt·imitiva, el acento caía en la última sílaba de la raíz y sus reflejos se notan en el amuzgo y en el trique; en otras, representadas por el cuicateco y el mixteco, el acento lo llevaba la penúltima sílaba. Actualmente, el mixteco tiene el acento en la posición referida, según observaciones hechas personalmente por la autora, en los diversos dialectos de la costa de Oaxaca.
new_statements.translation: In all other cases tone is not indicated, even though probably all the dialects have it. The proto-language surely had, besides tone, an accent on the root that distinguished it from the affixes. In some parts of the original dialect community the accent fell on the last syllable of the root, and its reflexes are seen in Amuzgo and Trique; in others, represented by Cuicatec and Mixtec, the penultimate syllable carried the accent. At present Mixtec has the accent in that position, according to observations made personally by the author in the various dialects of the Oaxaca coast.
new_statements.citation: Arana Osnaya, Evangelina. 1960. Relaciones internas del mixteco-trique. Anales del Instituto Nacional de Antropología e Historia XII (1959): 219-273. México: INAH. (Glottolog ref 415612; dialect sample p. 231 includes '(tm) San Juan Tamasola.. Dto. de Nochixtlán, Oax.', data collected by José Rendón, ENAH)
new_statements.locator: pp. 232-233 (section 2, Fonología, a); pp. 14-15; dialect list p. 231 (p. 13); see also p. 233 'Por estar relacionado el acento con una condición morfológica y no mecánicamente fonética, es necesario reconocer que es fonémicamente contrastante.. En las cuatro divisiones, el acento pudo omitirse, porque.. la posición del acento se desprende de las condiciones generales ya mencionadas' and p. 263 'acento inicial, en cuicateco y mixteco' (first syllable of the root); compounds p. 233: 'El elemento final lleva acento y el anterior o anteriores carecen de él.'
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: statement check: group-level-statement. Arana Osnaya 1960 states root-penultimate ('acento inicial' on the bisyllabic root) accent for Mixtec as a whole, explicitly 'segun observaciones hechas personalmente por la autora en los diversos dialectos de la costa de Oaxaca'; San Juan Tamazola (tm, Rendon/ENAH data) is only one of ~25 sample points and no Tamazola accent data are given (accent omitted in the forms). Identity of 'tm' = tama1339 is well established by the checker; the accent claim is family-level applied to, not observed on, Tamazola. morphologically determined/stress is the right encoding of that claim. | checker: Opened the mirror copy (56 pp, Adobe Paper Capture text, INAH Anale…
new_statements.relation_note: Section 2 (Fonología) reconstructs Proto-Mixteco-Trique segments; states root accent penultimate (= root-initial) for Mixtec and Cuicatec vs root-final for Trique and Amuzgo, accent morphologically bound to the root and phonemically contrastive, compounds final-member accented; tone assumed for all dialects but marked only where a phonemic analysis existed (not for Tamazola).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Mixtec (all dialects, as a division of Mixteco-Trique) carries the accent on the penultimate syllable of the root, i.e. the first syllable of the bisyllabic root/couplet ('acento inicial'), affixes being unaccented; in two-member compounds the final member carries the accent. Tone: probably present in all dialects but not transcribed for most, including the Tamazola (Rendón/ENAH) material.
new_statements.exceptions: compounds: accent on the final element, preceding element(s) unaccented (p. 233); accent marks omitted in the cited forms because position is predictable from the root
new_statements.identity_note: PASS-1 WORK, added: open copy located (INAH Anales OJS PDF, downloaded from the the Internet Archive because revistas.inah.gob.mx is could not be reached by automated download), read, and identity corrected - pass 1 had it record-only/print and the checker marked it 'another-variety'. The dialect list on p. 231 gives '(tm) San Juan Tamasola, (hu) Huitepec, Dto. de Nochixtlán, Oax. y (pe) Peñoles, Dto. de Etla, Oax., José Rendón (ENAH)'; San Juan Tamazola in the district of Nochixtlán is tama1339 [vmx] (Santiago Tamazola, the Baja town, is in Silacayoapan/Huajuapan, not Nochixtlán). Tamazola (tm.) figures in the lexicostatistic tables (tm. con sm. 81%, tm. con hu. 79%, etc.) and in 'grupo 3a' (p. 261). Glottolog attaches the reference to the parent node teoz1234. The accent statement itself is Mixtec-wide and Arana grounds it in her own observations of Costa dialects, not in the Tamazola list (see domain_note).

sources.citation: Mak, Cornelia & Robert Longacre. 1960. Proto-Mixtec phonology. International Journal of American Linguistics 26(1): 23-40.
sources.note: Comparative reconstruction of Proto-Mixtec segments and ultimate syllables from 28 modern dialects including San Juan Tamazola (dialect 5); tone is explicitly left out ('omitted the notation of tone in all citations'; PM tone not reconstructed) and the word 'stress' does not occur in the article; the only prosodic remark is the family-wide one that modern disyllabic morphemes carry a level tone on each vowel. Tamazola forms appear untonemarked in the cognate sets (wordlist-type data), so this is primary Tamazola segmental data but no stress or tone statement for the variety.
